A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
metabolic flux and essentiality, rather than network position, are the main factors that determine the rate of protein evolution.

the evolutionary rates of enzymes in the metabolic network of E. coli are determined by the fluxes of metabolites through the enzymes, and by the metabolic fluxes through the reactions catalyzed by the enzymes.
the evolutionary rate of an enzyme in the metabolic network of Escheichia coli is determined by its abundance and its metabolic function, but not its network position.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the evolutionary rate of a gene is not only determined by its position in the metabolic system, but also by its function in that system.
the evolutionary rate of an enzyme depends on its role in the function and organization of the metabolic network.
metabolic networks impose constraints on the evolution of their constituent enzymes, and that these constraints are more important than the network’s architecture.
